sections.title: Headline
sections.content: AI-agent infrastructure dominates today's GitHub Trending page: agent management, learned memory, model optimization, and AI-facing office automation occupy four of the top five positions. The broader list still includes foundational ML, developer tooling, security research, secrets management, and mobile automation.

sections.title: paperclipai/paperclip
sections.description: The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work

sections.title: NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer
sections.description: A unified library of SOTA model optimization techniques like quantization, distillation, pruning, neural architecture search, speculative decoding, etc.

sections.title: dream-num/univer
sections.description: The Office Harness for AI Agents — Spreadsheets, Docs, Slides, Canvas, Relational Tables, and PDF in one runtime.

sections.title: tensorflow/tensorflow
sections.description: An Open Source Machine Learning Framework for Everyone

sections.title: rohitg00/ai-engineering-from-scratch
sections.description: Learn it. Build it. Ship it for others.

sections.title: openbao/openbao
sections.description: Software for managing, storing, and distributing secrets, certificates, and keys.

sections.title: zhaoxuya520/reverse-skill
sections.description: AI-powered skill router and toolchain bootstrapper for authorized reverse engineering, penetration testing, and security research.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent operations and memory lead the snapshot; AI-native workspaces and inference efficiency are also prominent. TypeScript and Python are the leading languages among the ten listed repositories, with C++, Go, Rust, and PowerShell each appearing once.

sections.title: Notable Shifts
sections.content: The strongest shift is from standalone models toward systems around them: agent control planes, persistent memory, structured workspaces, deployment optimization, and security boundaries.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's trending signal is a systems story: the community is investing in making agents operational, stateful, useful across office workflows, and deployable at lower cost. Established infrastructure remains part of the stack.
